key_insight: A Bayesian finite element model reconstructs vascular velocity and pressure fields from sparse noisy measurements while quantifying uncertainty, without requiring offline training data.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable patient-specific flow diagnostics and downstream estimates such as pressure drop, flow rate, and wall shear stress for clinical decision-making.
method: Represent velocity and pressure with Taylor-Hood finite element basis functions.
Use physics-informed maximum-entropy priors plus a noise-model likelihood to form a posterior.
Compute MAP via sparse nonlinear least squares; eliminate pressure analytically and use Laplace approximation for uncertainty.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on patient-specific cerebral aneurysm, aortic aneurysm, and aortic coarctation geometries, where it outperformed tricubic interpolation and matched a PINN for field reconstruction while improving region-of-interest wall shear stress estimates.
watch_item: The approach depends on a steady-flow assumption and accurate geometry/noise modeling, and the Laplace approximation may underrepresent strongly non-Gaussian uncertainty.
paper_title: Bayesian finite element regression for vascular flow reconstruction with quantified uncertainty
